Title: Cisplatin ototoxicity in developing gerbils.
Target_Age: young gerbils (2 weeks of age at first exposure)
Stimulus_Type: cisplatin doses (one to three 5 mg/kg doses)
Outcome: DPOAE amplitude and ABR threshold elevation by cisplatin dose
Evidence_Quote: A tendency for a bimodal distribution of DPOAE and ABR responses was also observed in the D1 group, at frequencies below 8 kHz.

Title: Moderate noise trauma in juvenile cats results in profound cortical topographic map changes in adulthood.
Target_Age: 5-week-old kittens
Stimulus_Type: loud 6 kHz pure-tone exposure
Outcome: reorganization of the auditory cortex frequency map
Evidence_Quote: The present study demonstrates that exposure of 5-week-old kittens to a loud 6 kHz tone, producing mild to moderate high-frequency hearing loss, induces a profound reorganization of the frequency map in auditory cortex.

Title: Gender differences among newborns on a transient otoacoustic emissions test for hearing.
Target_Age: healthy full-term newborns (38-42 weeks gestation), first 48 hours of life
Stimulus_Type: transient evoked otoacoustic emission (TEOAE) click stimulus
Outcome: gender and frequency differences in TEOAE responses (cochlear sensitivity)
Evidence_Quote: During this test, a sudden burst of sound is presented at between 78 and 83 dB SPL which stimulates the entire basilar membrane.

Title: Binaural masking level differences in infants with and without otitis media with effusion.
Target_Age: infants aged 7-10 months (with or without otitis media with effusion)
Stimulus_Type: 500 Hz tone signal against narrowband noise masker (binaural masking)
Outcome: masked thresholds and binaural masking level differences
Evidence_Quote: Subjects were trained to detect a 500 Hz signal (either in or out-of-phase between the ears) against an in-phase, narrow band noise masker centred at 500 Hz.

Title: Middle ear and cochlear disorders result in different DPOAE growth behaviour: implications for the differentiation of sound conductive and cochlear hearing loss.
Target_Age: guinea pigs (age not stated)
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2 between 2.0 and 8.0 kHz)
Outcome: DPOAE I/O-function growth behaviour in middle-ear vs cochlear disorders
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE I/O-functions were recorded in a wide primary tone level range at up to 8 f2 frequencies between 2.0 and 8.0 kHz (15 dB SPL < L2< 60 dB SPL; L1=0.46 L2 + 41 dB SPL; f2/f1=1.2) in guinea pigs

Title: Prevalence of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 100 neonates and 50 normal-hearing young adults
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAE) recording
Outcome: SOAE prevalence, frequency ranges and average levels
Evidence_Quote: The majority of adult SOAEs are between 1.0 and 2.0 kHz, whereas the majority of neonatal SOAEs are between 2.5 and 5.0 kHz. The average SOAE level is -2.6 dB SPL for adults and 8.5 dB SPL for infants.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions for hearing threshold estimation and differentiation between middle-ear and cochlear disorders in neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: neonates (mean age 3.2 days; follow-up at 4 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (11 test frequencies, f2 = 1.5-8 kHz)
Outcome: hearing threshold estimation; differentiation of middle-ear vs cochlear disorders
Evidence_Quote: DPOAEs were measured in neonates after birth (mean age = 3.2 days) and 4 weeks later (follow-up) at 11 test frequencies between f2 = 1.5 and 8 kHz and compared to that found in normal hearing subjects and cochlear hearing loss patients.

Title: A retrospective study of the spectral probability of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions: rise of octave shifted second mode after infancy.
Target_Age: neonates, children (5-11 y) and adults (296 subjects across three surveys)
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emission (SOAE) recordings
Outcome: SOAE frequency distribution (spectral probability) by age group
Evidence_Quote: Neonates show a monomodal distribution with a peak at 4 kHz, but both children (5-11 y) and adults show an identical bimodal distribution, with two peaks in an octave distance (1.5 and 3 kHz).

Title: Noise in contemporary neonatal intensive care.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no human subjects (sound surveys in two neonatal intensive care units)
Stimulus_Type: NICU ambient sound (weekly sound surveys)
Outcome: equivalent sound pressure levels (LEQ) compared with recommended limits
Evidence_Quote: Median weekly equivalent sound pressure levels (LEQ) for NICU A ranged from 61 to 63 dB (A weighted), depending on the level of care. NICU B L(EQ) measurements ranged from 55 to 60 dB (A weighted).

Title: Pure-tone overstimulation protects surviving avian hair cells from acoustic trauma.
Target_Age: chicks (age not stated)
Stimulus_Type: intense pure-tone exposures (1.5 kHz and 2.2 kHz at 124 dB SPL)
Outcome: hair cell and tectorial membrane damage; protection from second exposure
Evidence_Quote: Chicks were exposed to a pure-tone of 1.5 kHz at 124 dB SPL. Lesion was found in both TM and hair cells, but the area of damage to the TM was much larger than that to the hair cells. Following this exposure, chicks were exposed to a second intense pure-tone at 2.2 kHz 124 dB SPL.

Title: Effects of temporal uncertainty and temporal expectancy on infants' auditory sensitivity.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants and adults
Stimulus_Type: 1 kHz tone in broadband noise (with/without acoustic cue)
Outcome: masked detection sensitivity under temporal uncertainty/expectancy
Evidence_Quote: In the present experiment, the effects of temporal uncertainty and temporal expectancy on infants' and adults' detection of a 1 kHz tone in a broadband noise were examined.

Title: The effect of decibel level of music stimuli and gender on head circumference and physiological responses of premature infants in the NICU.
Target_Age: premature infants in the NICU (gestational ages 28-33 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: lullaby and classical music presented at 65, 70 or 75 dB
Outcome: head circumference growth; heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation
Evidence_Quote: One quarter of the males and one quarter of the females listened to music presented at an average of 65 dB, one quarter at an average of 70 dB, one quarter at an average of 75 dB, and one quarter did not listen to any music and served as control subjects.

Title: Neuronal responses in chinchilla auditory cortex after postnatal exposure to frequency-modulated tones.
Target_Age: newborn chinchilla pups (exposure 4 weeks; tested at P28)
Stimulus_Type: continuous upward linear FM sweep exposure (0.1-20 kHz)
Outcome: cortical neuronal responses to pure tones and FM sweeps
Evidence_Quote: Newborn chinchilla pups were exposed continuously to an upward linear FM sweep (0.1-20 kHz) at 0.05 kHz/ms for 4 weeks.

Title: The breaking of cochlear scaling symmetry in human newborns and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human newborns and adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE swept-tone protocol (0.5 to 4 kHz segments)
Outcome: DPOAE phase-frequency functions; breaking of cochlear scaling symmetry
Evidence_Quote: In this study, DPOAE phase was recorded with a swept-tone protocol in three, octave-wide segments from 0.5 to 4 kHz.

Title: Processing simultaneous auditory objects: infants' ability to detect mistuning in harmonic complexes.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 6-month-old infants (adult thresholds also measured)
Stimulus_Type: harmonic complex tone (240 Hz fundamental, third harmonic mistuned)
Outcome: discrimination of mistuned harmonic complex (auditory object segregation)
Evidence_Quote: The present study used a conditioned head-turn procedure to examine whether 6-month-old infants are able to discriminate a complex tone (240 Hz, 500 ms, six harmonics in random phase with a 6 dB roll-off per octave) from a version with the third harmonic mistuned.

Title: Maturation of the human medial efferent reflex revisited.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: premature and term-born neonates, 6-month-old infants, young adults
Stimulus_Type: contralateral acoustic stimulation (CAS) during DPOAE recording
Outcome: MOC reflex strength (DPOAE amplitude/phase shifts) by age
Evidence_Quote: For all ages, the MOC reflex was strongest at frequencies below 1.5 kHz, and the reflection component of the DPOAE was most affected, showing maximally reduced amplitude and shallower phase slope when contralateral noise was presented.

Title: Distortion-product otoacoustic emission reflection-component delays and cochlear tuning: estimates from across the human lifespan.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 184 subjects from prematurely born neonates to elderly adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (2f1-f2) recording, 0.5-4 kHz (extended to 8 kHz in young adults)
Outcome: reflection-component delays and cochlear tuning estimates across the lifespan
Evidence_Quote: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs) at 2f1-f2 were recorded, and their reflection components were extracted in 184 subjects ranging in age from prematurely born neonates to elderly adults. DPOAEs were measured from 0.5-4 kHz in all age groups and extended to 8 kHz in young adults.

Title: Procedures for ambient-pressure and tympanometric tests of aural acoustic reflectance and admittance in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human adults and infants (1 month of age)
Stimulus_Type: aural acoustic reflectance and admittance measurement (0.2 to 8 kHz)
Outcome: reflectance/admittance measurement procedures and illustrative normal-ear data
Evidence_Quote: Procedures are described to measure acoustic reflectance and admittance in human adult and infant ears at frequencies from 0.2 to 8 kHz.

Title: Recovery of auditory function following intense sound exposure in the neonatal chick.
Target_Age: one-day-old chicks
Stimulus_Type: intense pure-tone exposure (0.9 kHz at 120 dB for 48 h)
Outcome: recovery of auditory thresholds and frequency selectivity (Q10 dB)
Evidence_Quote: One day old chicks were exposed to a 0.9 kHz tone for 48 h at 120 dB.

Title: Cortical plasticity with bimodal hearing in children with asymmetric hearing loss.
Target_Age: children with asymmetric hearing loss (implanted at 8.7 +/- 5.1 years)
Stimulus_Type: monaural acoustic click trains / biphasic electric pulses via cochlear implant
Outcome: cortical lateralization and aural preference; reversal with implant use
Evidence_Quote: Monaurally presented stimuli consisted of 36 ms trains of 9 acoustic clicks/biphasic electric pulses at a rate of 250 Hz, repeated at 1 Hz.

Title: Amplitude modulation detection and temporal modulation cutoff frequency in normal hearing infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: three-month-old infants and young adults (normal hearing)
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated broadband noise
Outcome: modulation detection threshold (MDT) and temporal modulation cutoff frequency
Evidence_Quote: The modulation detection threshold (MDT) of a broadband noise amplitude modulated at 10 Hz estimated the y-intercept of the TMTF. The cutoff frequency of the TMTF, measured at a modulation depth 4 dB greater than the MDT, provided an estimate of temporal resolution.

Title: Context matters: Cortical rhythms in infants across baseline and play.
Target_Age: 55 infants aged 6- to 12-months
Stimulus_Type: dynamic audiovisual display (baseline) and object play with mother; EEG recording
Outcome: EEG theta, alpha, beta and gamma power by context and scalp site
Evidence_Quote: Theta (3-6 Hz) and alpha (6-9 Hz) power were higher at frontal sites (Fp1/Fp2) during play relative to baseline. Beta (9-30 Hz) and gamma (30-50 Hz) power were higher at frontal (Fp1/Fp2) and frontal medial sites (F3/F4) during baseline relative to play.

Title: Acoustic analyses of infant fricative and trill vocalizations.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants aged 3, 6, 9, and 12 months
Stimulus_Type: infant fricative and trill vocalizations (recorded)
Outcome: spectral components and trill rates of infant closants
Evidence_Quote: Closants, or consonantlike sounds in infant vocalizations, were described acoustically using 16-kHz spectrograms and LPC or FFT analyses based on waveforms sampled at 20 or 40 kHz.

Title: Effects of an enhanced acoustic environment on residual hearing following chronic cochlear implantation and electrical stimulation in the partially deafened cat.
Target_Age: cats (neonatal aminoglycoside partially deafened model)
Stimulus_Type: enhanced acoustic environment: 80 dB SPL 4-talker babble, 14 h per day
Outcome: auditory thresholds and cochlear histology after chronic implantation and electrical stimulation
Evidence_Quote: To simulate potential over stimulation via a hearing aid, one cohort of animals were also exposed to an enhanced acoustic environment consisting of 80 dB SPL 4-talker babble presented 14 h per day.

Title: Changes in middle-ear input admittance during postnatal auditory development in chicks.
Target_Age: 73 chicks, 1-150 days post-hatch
Stimulus_Type: sound pressure measurements at the tympanic membrane (7 frequencies, 0.66-1.8 kHz)
Outcome: middle-ear input admittance magnitude and angle development
Evidence_Quote: Admittance at 7 frequencies (0.66-1.8 kHz) was calculated from measurements of the magnitude and phase angle of sound pressure in front of the tympanic membrane.

Title: Maternal vocalisations and other sounds in the fetal lamb's sound environment.
Target_Age: pregnant ewes and fetal lambs (last 3 weeks of gestation)
Stimulus_Type: maternal vocalisations and other sounds recorded in the amniotic sac; playback of ewe bleats
Outcome: attenuation of external sounds across gestation; lamb heart-rate responses to maternal vs alien bleats
Evidence_Quote: Over the last 3 weeks of gestation the attenuation of sounds from outside the mother decreased at frequencies between 500 and 4000 Hz, but not below or above those frequencies.

Title: Age-dependent effects of a pure tone trauma in the chick basilar papilla: evidence for a development of the tonotopic organization.
Target_Age: chicks and chick embryos (embryonic days 18/20; post-hatch days 1-30)
Stimulus_Type: 1.5 kHz pure tone at 125 dB SPL for 12 h
Outcome: frequency of maximum threshold elevation; basilar papilla damage position
Evidence_Quote: 58 chicks or chick embryos were continuously exposed during 12 h on either embryonic day 18 or 20 or on post-hatching days 1, 10, 20 or 30 to 1.5 kHz pure tone at an intensity of 125 dB SPL.

Title: Consistency and variability in pitch and tempo in infants' everyday musical lives.
Target_Age: 27 infants (home auditory environments)
Stimulus_Type: live song renditions by singers in the infant's environment
Outcome: consistency and variability of starting tonic pitches and average tempos
Evidence_Quote: singing a pop song 30 bpm and six semitones apart)

Title: Maturational and degenerative processes in the organ of Corti after neonatal hypothyroidism.
Target_Age: rats (propylthiouracil during first 30 days after birth)
Stimulus_Type: neonatal hypothyroidism (PTU); BAER and electrocochleography testing
Outcome: elevated auditory thresholds; organ of Corti maturation and degeneration
Evidence_Quote: Maturation of auditory potentials was achieved within 10-15 days but was incomplete since the animals definitely demonstrated elevated thresholds around 60-70 dB SPL.

Title: Acoustical properties of the human skull.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human skull specimens (fresh and formalin-immersed; no living subjects)
Stimulus_Type: focused ultrasound beam transmitted through skull sections
Outcome: insertion loss, reflection loss and sound speed of the skull
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made in the frequency range from 0.25 to 6 MHz. Most studies were restricted to an upper frequency limit of 2.2 MHz.

Title: Filtering and spectral characteristics of averaged auditory brain-stem response and background noise in infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: full-term infants
Stimulus_Type: clicks and 500-Hz tone bursts for ABR; 30-Hz vs 100-Hz high-pass recording filters
Outcome: ABR amplitude and Fsp; spectra of averaged ABR and background noise
Evidence_Quote: This study compares the effects of 30- and 100-Hz high-pass filters on ABR amplitude and response Fsp in full-term infants. Stimuli used to elicit ABRs are moderate- and low-level clicks and 500-Hz tone bursts.

Title: Frequency contribution to the click-evoked auditory brain-stem response in human adults and infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 3-month-old infants and adults (normal hearing)
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli with notched-noise masking (center frequencies 500-8000 Hz)
Outcome: ABR wave I and V latency and morphology by masker frequency
Evidence_Quote: Results indicate that 3-month-old infants have adultlike latency shifts (re: unmasked latency) when the ABR is recorded in the presence of notched-noise masking with center frequencies ranging from 500-8000 Hz.

Title: Changes in the cat cochlear nucleus following neonatal deafening and chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation.
Target_Age: cats (neonatally deafened kittens; implanted at 8-16 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation; ABR and frequency following response testing
Outcome: cochlear nucleus volume, spherical cell area and density
Evidence_Quote: Profound hearing loss was confirmed in each animal by auditory brainstem response (ABR) and frequency following response (500 Hz) testing. Five of the kittens were implanted unilaterally with a scala tympani electrode array at ages 8-16 weeks. These kittens were stimulated daily for four hours at 2 dB above the evoked ABR threshold, over a period of three months

Title: The sensitivity to 3,3'-iminodipropionitrile differs for high- and midfrequency hearing loss in the developing rat.
Target_Age: developing rats (IDPN exposure gestational day 15 to postnatal day 72; tested as adults)
Stimulus_Type: 5- and 40-kHz tones (reflex modification audiometry); IDPN exposure
Outcome: auditory thresholds; frequency-selective hearing loss by exposure age
Evidence_Quote: All animals were tested as adults for auditory thresholds to 5- and 40-kHz tones using reflex modification audiometry.

Title: Ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants aged 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months, and adults
Stimulus_Type: ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient measurement (125-10,700 Hz)
Outcome: ear-canal input impedance and reflection coefficient development
Evidence_Quote: The ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient were measured in an adult group and in groups of infants of age 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months over frequency range 125-10,700 Hz.

Title: Amplitude-modulation following response (AMFR): effects of modulation rate, carrier frequency, age, and state.
Target_Age: 1-month-old infants and adults
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated tones (carriers 500 and 2000 Hz)
Outcome: AMFR coherence; optimal modulation rate by age and state
Evidence_Quote: Stimulus AM rate was varied between 10 and 80 Hz for continuous tonal stimuli of 500 Hz, and between 20 and 80 Hz for continuous tonal stimuli of 2000 Hz.

Title: Coherence analysis of envelope-following responses (EFRs) and frequency-following responses (FFRs) in infants and adults.
Target_Age: 1-month-old infants and adults
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated tones
Outcome: FFR and EFR coherence growth and thresholds
Evidence_Quote: 'Best frequency' (i.e., infant 80 Hz and adult 40 Hz) EFR thresholds were the same for infants and adults at 500 and 1000 Hz, but infant EFR thresholds were poorer than adult thresholds at 2000 Hz.

Title: Thyroxine affects physiological and morphological development of the ear.
Target_Age: neonatal rat pups (hyperthyroid and control)
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (DPE) and ABR recording; thyroxine-induced hyperthyroidism
Outcome: onset and maturation of DPEs and ABR thresholds
Evidence_Quote: DPEs were recorded at an earlier postnatal age to high (8 kHz) frequencies and progressed to lower (3 kHz) frequencies with age.

Title: The effect of the evanescent wave upon acoustic measurements in the human ear canal.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no subjects (theoretical predictions for human ear canals; adults and 1-month-old infants referenced)
Stimulus_Type: acoustic measurement in the ear canal with loudspeaker and microphone (theory)
Outcome: predicted maximum evanescent-wave measurement error
Evidence_Quote: The maximum measurement error due to the presence of the evanescent wave in human ear canals below 10 kHz is predicted to be 3 dB in adults and 1.3 dB in 1 month old infants, when the loudspeaker and microphone ports are spaced more than 2 mm apart.

Title: Cochlear pathology induced by aminoglycoside ototoxicity during postnatal maturation in cats.
Target_Age: young kittens (15-24 days postnatal)
Stimulus_Type: neomycin sulfate (aminoglycoside) administration
Outcome: cochlear hair cell and spiral ganglion degeneration patterns
Evidence_Quote: In contrast, the spiral ganglion exhibited a different pattern of degeneration with initial cell loss occurring in the middle of the cochlea, about 40-60% from the base (approximately 2.8-8 kHz).

Title: Development of auditory function in the tammar wallaby Macropus eugenii.
Target_Age: tammar wallaby pouch young (95 to >180 days)
Stimulus_Type: click and tone burst stimuli by bone and air conduction (ABR)
Outcome: ABR thresholds and latencies across pouch development
Evidence_Quote: Thresholds to tone bursts in the centre frequency range (4-12 kHz) remained less than those for low (0.5-1.5 kHz) and higher (16 kHz) frequencies.
